hints.title: Complete Tree Depth Comparison Obstacle
hints.text: In a complete tree, every level except possibly the last is full, and last level leaves are as left as possible. How can comparing the left and right boundary depths determine if a subtree is completely full?

hints.title: Full Tree Formula Invariant
hints.text: If the leftmost depth equals the rightmost depth, the tree is a full binary tree with (2^h - 1) nodes. Otherwise, the count is 1 plus the counts of left and right subtrees.

hints.title: Subtree Boundary Halving Procedure
hints.text: Compute left boundary depth by following left pointers. Compute right boundary depth by following right pointers. If depths match, return (1 << depth) - 1. Otherwise, recursively return 1 + countNodes(root.left) + countNodes(root.right).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in complete tree (0 <= N <= 5 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: At each recursive level, at least one of the two subtrees is guaranteed to be perfectly full, pruning execution to O(log^2 N).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Counting nodes naively with standard traversal takes linear O(N) time without exploiting the complete tree property.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(log N) stack depth for logarithmic subproblem branching.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using bitwise shift (1 << depth) - 1 when boundary depths match.
